newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA 1996 FUNDS RETURNS ABOVE INFLATION - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA 1996 FUNDS RETURNS ABOVE INFLATION - SURVEY.

text.p: South African pension and provident funds showed an average return of 10.3 percent in 1996, just above the inflation rate of 9.4 percent, a survey said on Thursday.
The Consulting Actuaries Survey looked at 234 funds with assets totalling 226 billion rand.
The overall market value of assets in the survey was 19 percent higher than in 1995, partly due to new funds entering the report.
The report also showed that a trend of moving out of interest sensitive assets such as cash and bonds and into equities was continuing.

In 1996 interest sensitive assets made up 29.3 percent of the funds' assets, compared to a 1987 figure of 43.6 percent. Now equities make up 62.4 percent of the assets surveyed, with property making up 7.3 percent and overseas assets one percent.

"Once again last year the weighting towards fixed interest stocks decreased, continuing the trend of the past decade," said Philip Croeser, director of consultants Ginsburg, Malan & Carsons who helped conduct the survey.
The trend began when legislation obliging retirement funds to hold a large portion of their assets in fixed interest securities was removed in 1989.
In 1996 the bonds market did not perform well with the all-bond index giving a return of only 6.7 percent including income.
However, despite the trend towards more equity holdings the survey said that individual funds could still perform poorly if they invested too heavily in ailing stocks.
This was shown by a strong rise in energy firm Sasol's share price of 90.7 percent, while fellow blue chip stock industrial holding firm Murray & Roberts saw a drop of 58.1 percent.
